rulings.jobRole: Job Role authority IS implemented in PostgreSQL (EMP-RT-08) and is NOT a column on eos_workforce.employees and never will be. Migration 1760011200000 created eos_workforce.job_roles (the tenant catalog) and eos_workforce.employee_job_role_assignments (one current role per Employee, history kept), and functions/src/eosWorkforce/commands/employeeJobRoleCommands.ts is the governed writer -- createJobRole, updateJobRole, assignEmployeeJobRole, each requiring admin.employeeJobRole.write. Both tables hold 0 rows in nonprod (measured 2026-09-24), so Job Role carries no live authority yet and every jobRole value in this manifest is still seed metadata as far as THIS seed is concerned: seedSampleCompany.js writes no job role and a test asserts it names no job_role column. The catalog and the assignments are planned and applied by scripts/sampleCompany/personaAuthorityDimensions.js through the governed writers, never by a direct insert.
rulings.jobRoleIsNotSecurityRole: Job Role and Security Role are independent. No Security Role is derived from a Job Role and no Job Role is derived from a Security Role. Both are declared explicitly, per persona.

rulings.identityChain: Credential -> Principal -> governed tenant membership -> governed Employee/Principal link -> Employee. A Firebase uid is never an Employee id. Employee != User Access. Credential != Principal != Employee.
rulings.principals: Seeded Principals use the identity provider `eos-synthetic-nonprod`, which NO authentication verifier recognizes, so they can never sign in. They exist to exercise governed Principal / membership / Role-assignment / Employee-link relationships. The ONE real administrator Principal is REUSED, never recreated and never re-credentialed.
rulings.responsibility: Record Owner, Accountable Person and Assigned Person are three distinct facts and are never collapsed. Ownership is owner_employee_id; accountability is the governed establishment + mint; assignment has no PostgreSQL authority in any domain this manifest touches and is therefore never written.
rulings.accountability: GOVERNED/SEED: accountable_employee_id is persisted only from the value the governed establishment + mint produced, in the same transaction as the record, and only while it is still NULL. This is not live write activation and does not close activation blocker #2.
rulings.catalogWriterState: functions/src/catalogMaster/catalogWriterState.ts declares CATALOG_WRITER_AUTHORITY = { firestore: OPEN, postgres: INACTIVE }. rulings.firebase: Firebase is transitional credential entry only. This seed opens no Firebase connection, creates no Firestore document, and declares no Firebase business authority.
rulings.runtimeIdentityProvider: THE RUNTIME PROVIDER IS `firebase`, MEASURED NOT GUESSED. functions/src/eosApi/server.ts:101 reads `identityProvider: (env.EOS_IDENTITY_PROVIDER ?? "firebase").trim()`; :111-124 createFirebaseTokenVerifier returns `{ externalSubject: decoded.uid, identityProvider }` and reads ONLY the uid, never a custom claim; that pair goes straight into resolveOperationalContext -> resolvePrincipalContext, which looks the Principal up by (identity_provider, external_subject). render.yaml's eos-api-nonprod service does NOT set EOS_IDENTITY_PROVIDER, so the default `firebase` applies, and its GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT is eos-platform-sandbox. functions/src/adminPolicy/principalContext.ts:38 declares FIREBASE_IDENTITY_PROVIDER = "firebase".
rulings.firebaseIsIdentityOnly: Firebase Auth is TRANSITIONAL IDENTITY AND SESSION ONLY. It is never Employee authority, Security Role authority, capability authority, profile authority, ownership authority, workflow authority or any other business persistence. A Firebase uid is ONLY a Principal's external subject and is NEVER an Employee id. The Sample Company credential path uses firebase-admin/auth and is structurally forbidden from importing firebase-admin/firestore.

expectedAccess.$postgresCapabilityVocabulary_comment: THE GOVERNED POSTGRESQL CAPABILITY VOCABULARY, in full. eos_policy.capabilities is registered by migration, not by the in-repo Role catalog, and it currently holds these 79 ids and no others -- the newest THREE being receivingOrder.record.read, workOrder.record.read and reportDefinition.read, registered together by migration 1762300800000, THE AUTHORITY ACTIVATION VEHICLE. Owner ruling E requires a grant-bearing migration and the authority baseline that explains it to land as ONE change, so that migration also writes 26 Role grants and roleCapabilityAuthorityBaseline.json moved 387 -> 413 with it. The two record reads close a measured EDIT-WITHOUT-READ defect (ruling B): receivingOrder carried only inventory.stock.receive and workOrder carried only create/transition/three lifecycle actions, so both Objects had NO registered READ at all and thirteen Roles held a governed write on a record they could not read -- the READ verb was UNGOVERNED rather than withheld, which is a different fact and needed a registration rather than a grant. Each read is granted to exactly the Roles that hold the corresponding write, plus Owner, and confers no transition, dispatch, cancel, completion or receipt. reportDefinition.read is REPORTING SLICE 1 (ruling C): ONE Object-level read over saved report definitions, mirroring workflowDefinition, granted to admin, owner and reportViewer and to NO job-title Role. The 34 field-level report ids are deliberately NOT here: eos_policy.capabilities has object_key NOT NULL, UNIQUE (object_key, action_key) and no field column, so the relation cannot express a field dimension and field-level reporting belongs to eos_policy.role_field_permission_overrides. reportDefinition.delete is NOT REGISTERED, so it is ungrantable rather than merely ungranted, and reportFinanceViewer receives NO Object-level reporting capability because it is ADDITIVE finance-sensitive field visibility rather than a superset of reportViewer. Before those three, admin.securityPolicy.read, registered by migration 1762041600000 as the Administration READ authority: Administration > Objects, Roles & Permissions, Workflows, Permission Preview and Overview had no registered READ capability at all, and the `rolesPermissions` Object carried only admin.roleAssignment.write and admin.accessRequest.decide -- two ADMIN_ACTIONs -- so a navigation cutover could gate a read surface only on a write, making a reader indistinguishable from a writer. ONE Object-specific read was registered rather than a blanket administration.read: the Objects screen and the Roles & Permissions screen are two projections of the SAME stored authority over the SAME Object, and the four remaining Administration surfaces were ALREADY governed (admin.principalAccess.read for Users and the future Permission Preview, workflowDefinition.read for Workflows, audit.event.read for Audit Logs) while the Overview reads nothing governed and is answered by disjunction in code. Granted to exactly admin and owner, the population every other capability on the Administration authority Objects already has; workflowDefinition.read stays granted to NOBODY because Workflow Definition grant decisions are the Owner's and migrationChainSafety forbids a migration from making one. Before it, fulfillment.coordinatedVisit.read, which migration 1761955200000 REGISTERED rather than moved: the key existed only in the Firebase-era PERMISSION_CATALOG, and the governed seed pointed dispatchSchedule's R verb at it BY NAME while eos_policy.capabilities never carried the row. Retiring dispatchSchedule and notifications -- two Administration Objects over a record with no table, no collection and no document -- would have taken the one capability that governs something real down with them, so it is re-homed onto the Object whose state it reads (THE SALES ORDER IS THE COORDINATOR) as the BUSINESS_ACTION readCoordinatedVisits, never as a generic salesOrder READ. It is granted to exactly the five Roles the governed Role catalog already gives it and to no principal here; before that, inventory.manufacturer.read, split out of inventory.catalog.read by migration 1761782400000 so the capability names ONE Object (the Catalog read governed both Parts and Manufacturers, which a canonical capability cannot do); before that, the three keys added by migration 1761696000000 once the Owner ruled that whole-queue visibility is an Operational Scope and PARTS_ASSOCIATE is a Work Eligibility, so scope stopped needing to live in a capability key (reorder.request.read.queue is retained as SUPERSEDED migration evidence and may never be granted again); before that, the thirteen-key Finance, Administration and unconditioned Reorder vocabulary added by migration 1761609600000 (finance.read split into finance.invoice.read + finance.payment.read so a capability names ONE Object, the four named Finance acts registered as BUSINESS ACTIONS rather than minted as generic CRUD, and the three reorder keys that carry NO operationalRoleActive condition -- the conditioned ones are deliberately absent because role_capabilities has no scope column); before that, the eight-key CRED READ vocabulary added by migration 1761523200000, which registered the keys the CRUD matrix already used (inventory.catalog.read, warehouse.record.read, equipment.compatibility.view and five more) so the canonical model can finally express what role_object_permissions already enforces; migration 1761350400000 before it gave every capability its canonical object_key/action_key/action_kind/display_label so Administration can project security UNDER THE OBJECT (workOrder.cancel is deliberately NOT among them: workOrder.lifecycle.cancel already means it, and the new unique index on (object_key, action_key) now makes that duplication impossible) -- while PERMISSION_CATALOG holds several hundred. Every requiredCapabilities / forbiddenCapabilities id above is drawn from THIS list, because a capability the PostgreSQL authority does not know cannot be granted, cannot be resolved, and therefore cannot be proved either way. Role-catalog ids outside it are reported as CAPABILITY_VOCABULARY_PARTIAL rather than silently expected. The verifier asserts this list equals the live table, so a vocabulary migration is a reviewed change here.

owner-executive.$requiredCapabilities_comment: EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OMISSION. The `owner` Role's grant set is deliberately WITHHELD from this seed's capability reconciliation (expectedAccess.roleGrantScope), because reconciling it would grant `owner` every capability the compiled catalog declares for it and the compiled catalog declares `owner` and `admin` IDENTICALLY -- 151 permissions each, 60 of them inside the governed PostgreSQL vocabulary, with no difference in either direction. Live nonprod does NOT agree: `owner` holds 47 granted capabilities and `admin` holds 66, `owner` is a STRICT SUBSET, and 19 capabilities are admin-only. Running the reconciliation over `owner` would therefore close that gap by copying the Administrator's permissions onto the Owner, which the Owner ruling forbids by name. A required capability this seed refuses to grant may not be asserted as required, because in a freshly seeded tenant it would be a guaranteed false negative. What IS asserted is the pair of capabilities NO Role holds, and the separation itself is asserted structurally in roleGrantScope.measuredOwnerVsAdministrator.
owner-executive.$forbiddenCapabilities_comment: The Owner / Executive keeps the one assertion that a capability NOBODY holds must never start resolving. The 19 admin-only capabilities CANNOT be asserted forbidden here, because forbiddenCapabilities is validated against the COMPILED Role catalog and that catalog gives `owner` all of them. That divergence is itself the finding -- see blockedRelationships.OWNER_ROLE_CATALOG_EQUALS_ADMIN -- and it is declared rather than worked around by editing a Role definition.

expectedAccess.$gapClassification_comment: EVERY access finding carries EXACTLY ONE of the five governed classes. The class decides what may be done about it, which is why a vague 'gap' is not allowed to exist here: SEED_GRANT_GAP = the capability IS registered in eos_policy.capabilities and the Role catalog DOES declare it for this Role, but the live role_capabilities row is missing -- the governed reconciliation may add it. $principals_comment: TWO PRINCIPALS PER INTERACTIVE PERSONA, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM ACTIVE. `fixturePrincipal` is the v1 `eos-synthetic-nonprod` Principal, which NO verifier recognizes and which therefore cannot sign in; `loginPrincipal` is the real `firebase`-provider Principal the deployed runtime actually resolves. The activate-logins phase ensures the sandbox Auth account, resolves the Principal from its uid, REVOKES the fixture link through the governed lifecycle and establishes the login link -- never two simultaneous active links for one Employee, which the partial unique index makes structurally impossible anyway.

sandboxCredentials.accountPolicy: ABSENT -> create a passwordless sandbox-only Auth account. EXISTING -> REUSE; never delete and never recreate to reseed. MATERIALLY INCONSISTENT (disabled, or an email that is not the manifest's) -> FIXTURE_DRIFT and refuse.
sandboxCredentials.passwordPolicy: THE SAMPLE COMPANY GENERATES NO SECRET OF ITS OWN. --mode activate-credentials DELEGATES to activateMissingSandboxPasswords in functions/scripts/activateSandboxPersonas.js -- the same function that script's own --activate-missing CLI calls -- narrowed by an explicit allowlist to this manifest's interactive personas. Its semantics are unchanged: a strong random password ONLY for a persona that has none, every working persona left untouched, merged into the gitignored credential file rather than replacing it, an unparseable file refused. --rotate is REFUSED by name in the orchestrator and is unreachable through any Sample Company path.

The reused real Administrator is EXCLUDED -- its credential is real, pre-existing and out of scope, and its credentialEmail is null so it cannot become an allowlist entry. An @sandbox.invalid account outside the allowlist is never mutated; an allowlisted account that does not exist is REPORTED, never silently skipped.
sandboxCredentials.$canonicalRoleIdentityRegistry_comment: OWNER RULING 2026-09-25: ONE CANONICAL SANDBOX LOGIN PER CANONICAL JOB ROLE, and that registry -- not this manifest -- is the authority for which authentication identity a canonical persona uses. This block used to carry its own supersededIdentities map; it was removed because two copies of the same facts drift, and the symptom of drift here is an account created for an identity that already has one. functions/scripts/sampleCompany/credentialActivation.js derives activation eligibility from the registry file directly.

For ordinary fixture personas the two are deliberately equal and seedSampleCompany.js still enforces that. THREE canonical personas are the narrowly authorized exception, because their stable sandbox login intentionally differs from the synthetic Employee business email: dispatcher (workEmail emerson.fixture@, login dispatcher@), finance-controller (workEmail sage.fixture@, login acctmgr@) and restricted-user (workEmail wren.fixture@, login restricted@). NO workEmail WAS CHANGED to achieve this -- rewriting a person contact address to match an account is the data corruption the ruling forbids. The exception is granted by the registry and by nothing else; it is NOT a general permission for emails to differ.
